decisions.reason: F3 wrongly asserted C1 regularity of the differentiated PDE. C2 u makes p and f′(u)p C1, but their derivatives and f″(u) only continuous. The proof differentiates only the C1 product and composes the C1 p with a characteristic, so no higher regularity is needed. Corrected F3; checked mixed partials, transport and ODE interfaces, the reciprocal Riccati formula and interior continuation. Statement unchanged.

The cited integration-by-parts theorem is one-dimensional and cannot be restated as a theorem on balls. F4 now derives compact spatial integration by parts on coordinate slices of a box, transfers continuous slice integrals from Riemann to Lebesgue, and applies Fubini, twice for the Laplacian. Checked cutoff errors using finite L1 orbit bound, monotone dissipation and the L2 initial-time limit; defined M in the energy step. The full mass, norm and energy statement is unchanged.

The bracket in step 2.1 already equals -w div a; subtracting w eta-prime div a outside it counted that term twice. The outside divergence contribution is now eta div a, yielding exactly (eta-w eta-prime) div a minus the nonnegative viscous dissipation. Derived coordinate integration by parts with Fubini and the Riemann/Lebesgue bridge, and made the distributional time-cutoff passage explicit. Compact divergence bounds kill the delta error, finite L1 bounds kill the spatial cutoff errors, and L1 continuity includes 0 and T. Statement unchanged.

F1 incorrectly used the given essential-range constant in a theorem requiring a bound on the entire interval [-M,M]. The C1 hypothesis already provides the finite interval constant L-star=sup |f-prime| there; coordinate FTC proves its Lipschitz inequality. F1 and exhausting radii now use L-star internally, preserving the original claim and hypotheses. Countable null-set union and monotone exhaustion prove the almost-everywhere estimate; local L1 continuity passes each ball estimate to every time, including endpoints.

F3 falsely attributed signed essential extrema and least-bound attainment to an absolute-value norm definition. F3 now defines the signed infimum and supremum of essential bounds and proves attainment by the deterministic bounds M0+1/j and m0-1/j outside a countable union of null sets. It also proves max(|m0|,|M0|)=the essential norm. Constant solutions and comparison with an explicitly common finite bound give the range; Fubini and local L1 convergence give almost-every-time and every-time slices. Statement unchanged.

F2 asserted an unexported common time modulus for the derivatives, and step 2.1 used it without proof. Removed that assertion and proved instead a modulus CM sqrt(h)+Bh for W-epsilon using its restarted heat formula, spatial Lipschitz bound and Gaussian first moment. Uniform tails and local space-time L1 convergence give time-integrated global L1 convergence and global time continuity of the limit. The primitive norm is bounded by that L1 difference, and equicontinuity upgrades its time-integrated convergence to uniform convergence, licensing the viscosity contact argument. Mollification and localized constant-tail truncations retain both original correspondence classes and the -tf(0) normalization.

The original proof verified failure of the single shock but did not prove its additional composite-entropy-wave claim. Added the explicit shock at 3t/4 followed by -sqrt(x/(3t)) up to 3t. Checked its Rankine-Hugoniot coefficient, classical fan equation, continuous right attachment and 6t trace bound. The shock chord residual (z-1)(z+1/2)^2 is nonpositive; smooth convex inequalities and uniform approximation of Kruzhkov pairs prove entropy admissibility, and bounded-class uniqueness applies. The arc and tangent chord form the least concave majorant by derivative monotonicity and concavity of every competing majorant. Statement unchanged; no circular dependency on the later composite example.

F2 omitted the weak-solution premise of Rankine-Hugoniot and step 1.1 invoked it before weak solvability was established. F2 now states that premise, and step 1.1 first applies the existing strictly convex Riemann solver, whose exact hypotheses hold for the C2 quadratic flux and descending states. That theorem supplies the weak entropy shock and its chord speed; cancellation of the nonzero jump gives (uL+uR)/2. The later Lax/chord checks are now licensed, and the local trace error remains amplitude times |s|t, including a stationary shock. Statement unchanged.
